title: Dance Leap Tutorial I Center, Reverse, Firebird, Calyspo, Stag with @trainwithkendall

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher breaks down each leap step-by-step with guest dancers demonstrating. She uses encouraging commentary and visual imagery to explain body alignment.

lesson_structure.note: Demonstration of center, reverse, firebird, barreled calypso, and double stag leaps
Breakdown of the center leap with a student
Breakdown of the reverse leap with a second student
Breakdown of the firebird leap with the first student

cues: <short verbal cue the teacher repeats (<= 8 words)>
Start as low as you can
Spot the side you will be landing at
common_mistakes: Not squaring hips to the front
Crunching the head back on firebirds
safety: Start as low as you can and build up height

steps_taught.name: Center Leap
steps_taught.description: Chasse, step, leap off front foot with square hips and arms in T

steps_taught.name: Reverse Leap
steps_taught.description: Chasse, step, flip hips and leap with opposite foot forward

steps_taught.name: Firebird
steps_taught.description: Chasse, step, developpe with bent back leg and arched back

what_works: <what makes this lesson easy to absorb>
Detailed breakdown of mechanics like hip squaring and arm pathways
what_hinders: Multiple steps introduced quickly without much repetition of the full combination

quotes.text: You want to make sure wherever you're dancing that your hips are completely square to the front.
That left leg is the most important before you propel yourself upwards.
Your eye line tells your body where you'll be landing.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher stands beside the student, explaining foot placement and arm positions while the student performs a chasse and step.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact weight transfer details during fast movements

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates hip squaring and arm placement in a T shape.

extraction.distinctive_method: Breaking down leaps into specific pre-requisite elements like hip alignment and gaze direction before executing the full jump.
